hook.text: The 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster cost an estimated $700 billion. Insurance covered zero.

buildup.text: The Soviet Union had no insurance industry.

discovery.text: Western nations use nuclear pools to share reactor risk.

twist.text: No private insurer will fully cover a nuclear meltdown. The risk is too catastrophic and too rare to price accurately.

climax.text: Chernobyl proved nuclear energy's insurance problem: the risk is so extreme that only governments can backstop it.

quiz.question: Why was Chernobyl uninsured?
options: Soviet state-owned plants had no private insurance
